questions.question: What is the primary purpose of domain separation in ServiceNow?

options.text: To improve database query performance
To separate data, processes, and administrative tasks into logical groupings
To enable multiple users to log in simultaneously
To provide backup and disaster recovery capabilities

explanation.correct: Domain separation enables you to separate data, processes, and administrative tasks into logical groupings called domains. You can control several aspects of this separation, including which users can see and access data.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Performance optimization is not the primary purpose of domain separation; it's about data and process segregation for multi-tenancy
Multiple simultaneous logins are handled by standard platform capabilities, not domain separation
Backup and disaster recovery are separate platform features unrelated to domain separation

source.excerpt: Domain separation enables you to separate data, processes, and administrative tasks into logical groupings called domains.

questions.question: Which plugin must be activated to enable domain separation functionality in ServiceNow?

options.text: Domain Support — Domain Extension Installer
Service Provider Portal
Multi-Instance Management
Data Archive

explanation.correct: The Domain Support — Domain Extension Installer plugin must be activated to enable domain separation capabilities. This plugin adds the necessary infrastructure for creating and managing domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Provider Portal is a different feature for customer-facing portals, not domain separation infrastructure
Multi-Instance Management is for managing multiple ServiceNow instances, not domains within a single instance
Data Archive is for archiving old records, unrelated to domain separation

source.excerpt: If it is not already active, activate the Domain Support – Domain Extension Installer plugin.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid benefits of implementing domain separation for customers? (Choose three)

options.text: Enforce absolute data segregation between business entities
Customize business process definitions and user interfaces for each domain
Automatic database replication across data centers
Maintain some global processes and global reporting in a single instance
Eliminate the need for user authentication

explanation.correct: Domain separation is best for customers who need to: (1) enforce absolute data segregation between business entities (data separation), (2) customize business process definitions and user interfaces for each domain (delegated administration), and (3) maintain some global processes and global reporting in a single instance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Database replication is handled by infrastructure and high availability features, not domain separation
Domain separation does not affect authentication requirements; users still must authenticate to access the platform

source.excerpt: Domain separation is best for those customers who: Need to enforce absolute data segregation between business entities, Customize business process definitions and user interfaces for each domain, Maintain some global processes and global reporting in a single instance.

questions.question: When is using separate ServiceNow instances recommended instead of domain separation?

options.text: When you need to share reports across departments
When you need complete and total separation of all system properties and do not require global reporting
When you want to use a single login page for all users
When you want to reduce licensing costs

explanation.correct: If you need complete and total separation of all system properties and do not require global reporting or global processes, separate instances are the best option. Domain separation within a single instance still shares some global properties and processes.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Sharing reports across departments is actually easier with domain separation in a single instance
A single login page can be configured in both domain-separated and multi-instance scenarios
Licensing costs are not typically reduced by using separate instances; this is not a valid reason for choosing between approaches

source.excerpt: If you need complete and total separation of all system properties and do not require global reporting or global processes, separate instances are the best option.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the global domain and the TOP domain in ServiceNow?

options.text: They are the same domain
TOP is the root domain containing all records; global is a special domain for shared reference data
Global is higher than TOP in the hierarchy
They are unrelated concepts

explanation.correct: TOP is the root domain at the highest level of the domain hierarchy and contains all records. The global domain is a special domain used to store shared reference data (like system properties) that should be visible to all domains. Records in global domain are typically accessible from all domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: TOP and global are different domains with different purposes
TOP is the root; global exists alongside but serves a different purpose
They are both fundamental to domain separation architecture

source.excerpt: TOP domain is the root containing all records; global domain is for shared reference data visible to all

questions.question: Which property must be set to true to enable domain separation on a ServiceNow instance?

options.text: glide.sys.domain.enabled
glide.sys.domain.delegated_administration
glide.sys.domain.separation
glide.sys.domain.active

explanation.correct: The property glide.sys.domain.enabled must be set to true to activate domain separation on the instance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: glide.sys.domain.delegated_administration enables delegated admin but doesn't enable domain separation itself
This is not a valid ServiceNow property for domain separation
This is not a valid ServiceNow property for domain separation

questions.question: What is the domain hierarchy structure in ServiceNow?

options.text: A flat structure where all domains are equal
A tree structure with global at the root, TOP domain below it, and customer domains as children of TOP
A mesh network where all domains connect to each other
A two-level structure with only global and one customer domain

explanation.correct: ServiceNow domain separation uses a hierarchical tree structure: Global domain is the root, the TOP domain sits below global, and tenant/customer domains are created as children under TOP.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Domains are organized hierarchically, not as a flat structure
Domains follow a parent-child tree, not a mesh
Multiple levels and multiple customer domains are supported

questions.question: What is the significance of the TOP domain in ServiceNow domain separation?

options.text: It replaces the global domain
It serves as the parent domain for all tenant domains and is typically used by the service provider
It is only used for testing purposes
It automatically duplicates all global domain records

explanation.correct: The TOP domain is the service provider's domain that sits directly below global. All tenant/customer domains are created as children of TOP, and the service provider manages shared resources at this level.

wrongAnswers.explanation: TOP exists alongside global; global remains the root domain
TOP is a production domain used by the service provider
Records are not automatically duplicated between domains

questions.question: An MSP is setting up domain separation and needs to determine where shared configuration items like knowledge articles should reside. Where should they place shared content?

options.text: In each tenant domain individually
In the TOP or global domain so it is visible to all child domains
In a separate ServiceNow instance
In an external content management system

explanation.correct: Shared content should be placed in the TOP or global domain because domain separation visibility rules allow child domains to see records from parent domains by default.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Duplicating content in each domain creates maintenance overhead
Separate instances defeat the purpose of domain separation
External systems add unnecessary complexity for content that can be shared natively

questions.question: Which of the following is a prerequisite before enabling domain separation on a ServiceNow instance? (Choose two)

options.text: All existing data must be deleted
Careful planning of the domain hierarchy and data segregation strategy
Understanding which applications support domain separation
Upgrading to the latest ServiceNow release

explanation.correct: Before enabling domain separation, organizations must plan their domain hierarchy carefully and verify which applications support domain separation, as not all applications are domain-separation aware.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Existing data doesn't need to be deleted; it needs to be properly assigned to domains
While staying current is recommended, domain separation doesn't require the absolute latest release

questions.question: What happens to existing records when domain separation is first enabled on an instance?

options.text: All records are automatically deleted
Existing records remain in the global domain until explicitly reassigned
Records are randomly distributed across domains
The instance must be rebuilt from scratch

explanation.correct: When domain separation is enabled, existing records stay in the global domain. Administrators must then assign records to appropriate domains as part of the migration process.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Records are preserved; enabling domain separation is non-destructive
Records stay in global; they don't move automatically
Domain separation is enabled on existing instances without rebuilding

questions.question: What is delegated administration in the context of domain separation?

options.text: Allowing any user to administer any domain
Enabling domain-level administrators to manage users, groups, and configurations within their own domain
Removing the need for a global administrator
Automatically synchronizing admin settings across domains

explanation.correct: Delegated administration allows service providers to give tenant administrators control over their own domain's users, groups, and certain configurations without affecting other domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Delegated admin restricts administration to specific domains, not all domains
Global administrators are still needed for platform-level management
Settings are managed independently per domain, not synchronized

questions.question: A service provider needs to onboard a new customer tenant. Which steps are required? (Choose two)

options.text: Create a new ServiceNow instance for the customer
Create a new domain under the TOP domain for the customer
Assign appropriate users and groups to the new domain
Disable domain separation temporarily

explanation.correct: Onboarding a new tenant requires creating a child domain under TOP and assigning users/groups to that domain with appropriate roles.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Domain separation allows multiple tenants on a single instance
Domain separation should remain enabled; disabling it would affect all tenants

questions.question: Why is domain separation considered irreversible once enabled in production?

options.text: Because ServiceNow doesn't provide an uninstall option
Because the sys_domain field is added to many tables and data relationships become domain-dependent, making reversal extremely complex
Because it requires a special license that cannot be returned
Because other instances are automatically affected

explanation.correct: Once enabled, domain separation adds the sys_domain field to numerous tables and all data operations become domain-aware. Reversing this would require restructuring all domain-dependent data relationships.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While there's no simple toggle, the reason is the deep data impact
Licensing is separate from the technical irreversibility
Each instance is independently managed

questions.question: Which role is required to create and manage domains in ServiceNow?

options.text: itil
admin
domain_admin
user_admin

explanation.correct: The admin role is required to create and manage the domain hierarchy. Domain administrators (domain_admin) can manage within their domain but cannot create new domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The itil role is for ITSM users, not domain management
domain_admin can manage within a domain but cannot create new domains in the hierarchy
user_admin manages users but not the domain structure
